chunks: Muḥammad ibn Yaḥyā, from Saʿd ibn ʿAbd Allāh, from Ibrāhīm ibn Muḥammad al-Thaqafī, from ʿAlī ibn al-Muʿallā, from his brother Muḥammad, from Durust ibn Abī Manṣūr, from ʿAlī ibn Abī Ḥamzah, from Abū Baṣīr, from Abū ʿAbd Allāh عليه السلام, who said:

When the Prophet صلى الله عليه وآله was born, he remained for some days without any milk for him. So Abū Ṭālib placed him upon his own breast, and Allah caused milk to come into it; thus he suckled from him for some days, until Abū Ṭālib came upon Ḥalīmah al-Saʿdiyyah, and he handed him over to her.

key_terms.أَبُو طَالِبٍ: Abū Ṭālib, the Prophet’s guardian who cared for him in this report
key_terms.النَّبِيُّ: the Prophet صلى الله عليه وآله, the central figure whose infancy is being described
key_terms.ثَدْيِ: breast, the means through which the milk was provided
key_terms.حَلِيمَةَ السَّعْدِيَّةِ: Ḥalīmah al-Saʿdiyyah, the woman to whom the Prophet صلى الله عليه وآله was later entrusted
key_terms.لَبَنٌ: milk, the nourishment that was initially unavailable and then divinely provided

ai.seo_question: What does al-Kāfī narrate about how the Prophet صلى الله عليه وآله was nourished in his first days after birth?
ai.summary: This report describes an early event from the infancy of the Prophet صلى الله عليه وآله, relating that Allah provided nourishment for him through Abū Ṭālib before he was entrusted to Ḥalīmah al-Saʿdiyyah. The narration highlights divine care for the Prophet صلى الله عليه وآله and the protective role of his family in his earliest days.

en.hubeali:
Muhammad Bin yahya, from Sa’d Bin Abdullah, from Ibrahim Bin Muhammad Al Saqafy, from Ali Bin Al Moalla, from his brother Muhammad, from Dorost Bin Abu Mansour, from Ali Bin Abu Hamza, from Abu Baseer, 
(It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> having said:

‘When the (parents of) Prophet<sup>saww</sup> were blessed, he<sup>saww</sup> remained for days, there wasn’t any milk for him<sup>saww</sup>. So Abu Talib<sup>as</sup><sup>ws</sup> cast him<sup>saww</sup> upon his<sup>as</sup><sup>ws</sup> own breast, and Allah<sup>azwj</sup> Sent down milk from it. So he<sup>saww</sup> breast-fed from him<sup>as</sup><sup>ws</sup> for days until Abu Talib<sup>as</sup><sup>ws</sup> came to Haleema Saeeda, so he<sup>as</sup><sup>ws</sup> handed him<sup>saww</sup> over to her’.
en.sarwar: 26. Ali ibn Ibrahim has narrated from his father from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn abu Nasr from Rifa‘Abdallah from abu ‘Abdallah (a.s.) who has said the following.

“At a certain place around the Ka‘ba ‘Abd al-Muttalib’s people would spread house furnishings for him only and for no one else. His sons would stand around him for protection. Once the Messenger of Allah, then a small child who had just began to walk came to ‘Abd al-Muttalib and sat in his lap. One of the people standing as a guard came to remove the child away but ‘Abd al-Muttalib said, “Leave my child alone. The angel has just come to him.”
